goal: Half-year sales review of data/orders.json (Jan-Jun 2026): totals, regional breakdowns, top customers, monthly trend, refund behaviour by category, and product-level insights.

steps.title: Half-year totals and status mix
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS (use exactly): order revenue = quantity * unit_price. GROSS revenue = sum over ALL 400 orders regardless of status. NET revenue = sum over orders with status=='completed' only. AOV = NET revenue / number of completed orders.

Report for the whole Jan-Jun 2026 file, one line each, in this exact order and format:
TOTAL_ORDERS: <int>
COMPLETED: <int>
REFUNDED: <int>
CANCELLED: <int>
GROSS_REVENUE: <number rounded to 2 decimals>
NET_REVENUE: <number rounded to 2 decimals>
AOV: <number rounded to 2 decimals>
UNITS_COMPLETED: <int, sum of quantity over completed orders>

Write plain numbers with no currency symbol and no thousands separators.
steps.expected_result: TOTAL_ORDERS: 400; COMPLETED: 300; REFUNDED: 51; CANCELLED: 49; GROSS_REVENUE: 482245; NET_REVENUE: 350507; AOV: 1168.36; UNITS_COMPLETED: 814
steps.note: query_orders tool limited to 50 rows per region; no pagination/offset support; only retrieved 200/400 orders total
steps.result: s1: blocked - The mcp__plan__query_orders tool cannot retrieve all 400 orders required by the analysis. The tool is limited to 50 rows per query with a maximum region filter (AMER, EMEA, LATAM, APAC), providing only ~200 distinct orders across all available queries. Missing capability: pagination/offset parameters to retrieve remaining ~200 orders from the database.

steps.title: Regional breakdown of net revenue
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. NET revenue counts ONLY orders with status=='completed'.

For each of the 4 regions compute NET revenue, the number of completed orders, average order value (net revenue / completed orders) and the share of total net revenue in percent. Rank regions by NET revenue descending.

Output exactly 5 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals, no currency symbols:
<rank>. <REGION>: revenue=<x>, orders=<int>, aov=<x>, share=<x>%
(4 such lines, then)
LEADER: <REGION>

Example of the line format: '1. FOO: revenue=1234.5, orders=12, aov=102.88, share=30.12%'

steps.title: Top customers by net revenue
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. NET revenue counts ONLY orders with status=='completed'.

Rank all customers by NET revenue descending and report the top 5, plus the combined share of those top 5 against the TOTAL net revenue of all customers.

Output exactly 6 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals:
<rank>. <customer_id>: revenue=<x>, completed_orders=<int>
(5 such lines, then)
TOP5_SHARE: <x>%

Use the customer_id exactly as it appears in the data (e.g. C012).
steps.expected_result: 1. C007: revenue=18623, completed_orders=11; 2. C029: revenue=18610, completed_orders=10; 3. C036: revenue=15319, completed_orders=11; 4. C027: revenue=14998, completed_orders=13; 5. C005: revenue=13904, completed_orders=8; TOP5_SHARE: 23.24%
steps.note: Query tool limited to 50 rows maximum per query with no pagination support. Collected ~250 unique orders across all region-filtered queries, but dataset contains ~400+ orders based on order_id range (O0001-O0400+). Cannot reliably determine top 5 customers without complete dataset access. Tool capability missing: pagination or full-dataset export.
steps.result: s3: BLOCKED - Query API limited to 50 rows/query with no pagination. Complete H1 2026 dataset (~400+ orders) inaccessible. Top 5 customers calculation incomplete without full data access through either: (1) pagination in query tool, (2) date-range filtering, or (3) direct orders.json file read access.

steps.title: Monthly net revenue trend with month-over-month change
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. NET revenue counts ONLY orders with status=='completed'. Month = first 7 characters of the date field (YYYY-MM).

For each month from 2026-01 to 2026-06 report NET revenue, completed order count, and month-over-month change in percent versus the previous month ((cur - prev) / prev * 100). January has no previous month.

Output exactly 8 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals:
<YYYY-MM>: revenue=<x>, orders=<int>, mom=<x>%
(for 2026-01 use mom=n/a; 6 such lines, then)
BEST_MONTH: <YYYY-MM>
WORST_MONTH: <YYYY-MM>

BEST/WORST are by net revenue.
steps.note: Tool limitation: Cannot retrieve data beyond April 2026. Query limit is 50 rows per call with no pagination support. Regional queries show: EMEA ends 2026-03-05, AMER ends 2026-04-12, APAC ends 2026-03-27, LATAM ends 2026-04-04. No May-June data accessible.
steps.result: s4: BLOCKED - Cannot retrieve complete dataset for s4. The query_orders tool is limited to 50 rows per call with no pagination or date filtering. Regional queries returned data only through April 2026 (AMER max date: 2026-04-12). May and June 2026 data is not accessible within the tool's constraints. Task requires 6 months of data (Jan-Jun 2026) but only 4 months (Jan-Apr 2026) could be retrieved. Tool needs pagination support or date range filtering to complete the analysis.

steps.title: Refund behaviour by category
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. Refund rate for a group = (number of orders with status=='refunded' in the group) / (TOTAL number of orders in that group, all statuses) * 100. Refunded revenue = sum of revenue over refunded orders only.

For each of the 4 categories report total order count (all statuses), refunded order count, refund rate %, and refunded revenue. Rank by refund rate descending.

Output exactly 7 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals:
<rank>. <category>: orders=<int>, refunded=<int>, rate=<x>%, refunded_revenue=<x>
(4 such lines, then)
OVERALL_REFUND_RATE: <x>%
TOTAL_REFUNDED_REVENUE: <x>
WORST_CATEGORY: <category>

OVERALL_REFUND_RATE is over all 400 orders. WORST_CATEGORY is the one with the highest refund rate.
steps.expected_result: 1. services: orders=70, refunded=11, rate=15.71%, refunded_revenue=20030; 2. subscription: orders=91, refunded=13, rate=14.29%, refunded_revenue=13023; 3. hardware: orders=130, refunded=17, rate=13.08%, refunded_revenue=31230; 4. accessories: orders=109, refunded=10, rate=9.17%, refunded_revenue=2450; OVERALL_REFUND_RATE: 12.75%; TOTAL_REFUNDED_REVENUE: 66733; WORST_CATEGORY: services
steps.note: mcp__plan__query_orders API hard limit: max 50 rows per query, no pagination/offset parameter available. Can only access 50 unique orders (from first result batch) across all queries. Goal requires analysis of 400 orders for half-year review. Tool capability missing: pagination or offset parameter, or ability to read local data/orders.json file directly.
steps.result: s5: BLOCKED - Cannot complete refund behaviour by category analysis. The mcp__plan__query_orders function has a hard maximum limit of 50 rows per query with no pagination or offset capability. All attempts to retrieve data (regional queries, unfiltered queries, multiple sequential calls) return only the same first 50 orders. The analysis requires all 400 orders for the half-year (Jan-Jun 2026) to calculate accurate refund rates and totals by category. Missing tool capability: pagination support (offset parameter) or direct file access to data/orders.json.

steps.title: Product-level insights
steps.instructions:
DEFINITIONS: order revenue = quantity * unit_price. NET revenue counts ONLY orders with status=='completed'. Units = sum of quantity. Product AOV = net revenue / completed order count for that product.

Rank all products by NET revenue descending. Report the top 5 products, then the single lowest-revenue product, then the product with the most units sold, then net revenue per category.

Output exactly 11 lines, numbers rounded to 2 decimals:
<rank>. <product>: revenue=<x>, units=<int>, orders=<int>, aov=<x>
(5 such lines, then)
LOWEST_REVENUE_PRODUCT: <product> (<x>)
MOST_UNITS_PRODUCT: <product> (<int> units)
CATEGORY_REVENUE: <cat1>=<x>, <cat2>=<x>, <cat3>=<x>, <cat4>=<x>
(the CATEGORY_REVENUE list ordered by net revenue descending, on one line)

Report three blocks, numbers rounded to 2 decimals.

Block A - for each region (alphabetical: AMER, APAC, EMEA, LATAM) the top category by NET revenue and the top product by NET revenue:
<REGION>: top_category=<category> (<x>), top_product=<product> (<x>)

Block B - regions ranked by refund rate descending:
<rank>. <REGION>: refunded=<int>/<total int>, rate=<x>%

Block C - exactly three lines:
Q1_NET_REVENUE: <x>
Q2_NET_REVENUE: <x>
Q1_TO_Q2_CHANGE: <x>%
